title: Na-Dene languages - Wikipedia
text: Na-Dene is a family of Native American languages that includes at least the Athabaskan languages, Eyak, and Tlingit languages. Haida was formerly included but is now generally considered a language isolate.

title: Langues athapascanes — Wikipédia
text: Distribution pré-coloniale des langues na-déné (athapascanes + eyak + tlingit). Le terme athapascan ou athabascan[1], ainsi que le terme déné, désigne un vaste ensemble de peuples amérindiens et la famille de langues qu’ils parlent.

title: The Athabaskan Language Family - Native American Netroots
text: The Athabaskan (also spelled Athapaskan and Athabascan) language family is found in the western American Indian culture areas. Linguists feel that the Athabaskan language family is one branch of a larger genetic grouping called Athabaskan-Eyak.

title: Languages - Eyak | Alaska Native Language Center
text: Eyak is not an Athabascan language, but a coordinate sub-branch to Athabascan as a whole in the Athabascan-Eyak branch of the Athabascan-Eyak-Tlingit language family.

title: Athabaskan languages
text: Athabaskan (also spelled Athabascan, Athapaskan or Athapascan, and also known as Dene) is a large family of indigenous languages of North America, located in western North America in three groups of contiguous languages: Northern, Pacific Coast and Southern (or Apachean).

title: Pacific Coast Athabaskan languages Facts for Kids
text: Pacific Coast Athabascan. Subdivisions: California. Oregon. Pacific Coast Athabaskan is a geographical and possibly genealogical grouping of the Athabaskan language family.
